note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Thirteen of the fourteen divisions were filled by a single nomination and are listed from the nomination reports. In Glenmachiernan a contest was expected between Mr. John Hamilton and Mr. Hugh Osborne (the retiring member); the poll result was not traced in the papers available, so that division is not recorded here. Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Northern Whig, 6 May 1927, p. 7 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the name is cited to the 6 May report, as the 14 May reprint dropped this line. Renamed from 'Glenann' to Glenaan (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Glenaan; the rounds were filed as Glenann (1927, 1930); Glenaan (1933, 1936, 1955); Glenan (1939); Glenane (1946). This round was filed as 'Glenann', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (glenann) answers with a redirect to this one.
